prompt:
Create an illustrated science-fiction world with convincing three-dimensional depth and a hand-inked graphic-novel finish. Use strong silhouettes, expressive outlines, textured shadows and worn materials. Build environments from layered machinery, exposed pipes, suspended cables, overlapping panels and objects that suggest everyday use and repair. Organize dense detail around clear focal points. Use controlled colour palettes with warm luminous accents against cool shadow, giving each location its own atmosphere. The world should feel active, inhabited and larger than the visible frame, with layered depth, while the composition stays clear. Overall: lived-in, cyber, illustrated science fiction, lit and readable: warm lamplight against cool purple shadow, dark only in the corners. This is a still picture and code adds the motion, so paint everything crisply: no motion blur, no lens blur, no film grain.

Room B, the laboratory, in the same illustrated world: purple, lit warm. The whole room is one purple family, the colours of the attached guide: deep violet in the shadows and corners (#2A1446, #4B2079), turning to plum where the warm light falls (#582D59, #684166, #774B70), warmest closest to the lamps (#8C5675). The lamps' light is warm: cream at their cores (#FCE3A0) and an orange glow (#EC793C) on the walls, the ceiling and the deck around them. Walls, panels, pipes, cables and deck plates take their colour from that family; worn edges, rivets and plate seams show a little rust (#75402E); nothing is neutral grey, and nothing is tan, beige or olive. The shadows are deep violet, never black-brown or grey. Pale specimen glass; labels and paper are blank, in a warm paper white. Small indicator lights are blue-green (#3A9497); no other coloured light, and no green or blue light. Clinical and worn, quiet but lived in. The guide is the room's colour plan: paint over it in full detail and texture, but keep its colours and where its light falls.

This is a correction of the attached picture. Repaint only the masked shapes, and leave everything outside them exactly as it is. Each masked shape holds the furniture named for it, filling that shape exactly, standing on the deck, painted in full detail in the picture's style and light: the shape ahead holds two pieces, a low workbench that stands out from the east wall, seen at an angle, its top lit warm, with a microscope on its left end and, behind it on the right, a waist-high console with a slanted top whose display is plain and dark, with no readouts, bars or keys on it; the shape on the right is a low wheeled cart with shelves; the shape just right of it is a round stool on a single post with a ring of feet.

No people, and no words, letters or logos. Leave screens plain for the game to fill: openings marked black in the guide stay flat black and empty. No figures, faces, hands, silhouettes or animals; no signs, symbols or readable screens (any label is blank or abstract marks); no buttons or panels that look like game controls; no emblems, insignia, signature, watermark or border.
